AI Agent Architect, Customer Experience — Airtable

Date: Jun 15, 2026 | Location: Remote – US | Company: Airtable

About Airtable

Airtable is the no-code app platform that empowers people closest to the work to accelerate their most critical business processes. More than 500,000 organizations, including 80% of the Fortune 100, rely on Airtable to transform how work gets done.

Role Summary

Join Airtable as a CX AI Architect and own the technical foundation powering their AI-native customer support experience. Design and optimize how AI agents reason, retrieve, decide, and act — architecting knowledge systems, decision logic, and guardrails for reliable, scalable AI resolution.

Compensation

| Location | Salary Range (USD) |
|----------|-------------------|
| SF Bay Area, Seattle, NYC, LA | $196,000 – $278,100 |
| All other locations (incl. remote) | $177,000 – $250,300 |

Includes benefits, RSUs, potential incentive compensation.

Key Responsibilities

- Own Agent Retrieval Accuracy & Relevance: architect knowledge systems, measure/improve retrieval precision, contextual relevance, hallucination rates
- Drive Automated Resolution Rates: build decision frameworks, define API access and permissions, encode business logic into auditable, predictable systems
- Manage AI Safety & Trust: establish guardrails, prevent edge case errors and prompt injection, focus on what the agent doesn't do wrong
- Own the Feedback Loop: monitor observability layer, instrument retrieval accuracy and action success rates, drive week-over-week improvements
- Continuously Improve Agent Quality: develop prompt architecture, build versioning/A/B testing/performance evaluation systems
- Drive Integration Strategy: architect agent connections to external systems (billing, CRM, APIs), define authentication, error handling, data transformation

Ideal Candidate Profile

- LLM Expertise: understands how LLMs work — reasoning, failure modes, underlying mechanics; RAG, prompt engineering, chain-of-thought, agent frameworks; built production AI systems
- Systems Thinking: designs complex reliable systems using data flows, state management, error handling, edge cases
- Technical Prototyping: can write scripts, work with APIs, query databases, prototype solutions
- Data-Driven & Observability-Focused: instruments systems, analyzes logs, builds dashboards, defines metrics
- Strong Communication: explains complex AI behavior to non-technical stakeholders, writes clear documentation, effective cross-functional collaborator

Notes

- Cover letter required
- Applied: 2026-06-15
- Resume: Kara_Novotny_Resume_Airtable.html
- Cover letter: Kara_Novotny_Cover_Letter_Airtable.html

materials.cover_letter:
You are looking for someone to own retrieval accuracy, safety guardrails, and automated resolution rates. I build AI agents and the evaluation systems to know if they actually work. That is the job, and I have been doing it for seven years.

At Redwood, I built FlareGuard, an AI content validation workflow with automated benchmarks and quality scoring. It cut escalations by 70-80% and stopped incorrect output from reaching production. I went after the failure modes directly: structured guardrails, fallback paths, and post-processing checks that catch hallucination before a customer sees it. I also redesigned a 200-article help portal with role-aware navigation and built a PDF pipeline that solved a years-long customer complaint. That work is the same job as yours: define what the agent does right, measure it, and catch it when it goes wrong.

I want to build this at Airtable because your agents act inside real workflows, on real customer data, and the cost of a bad action is high. I design prompt architectures, version and A/B test them, and instrument retrieval accuracy and action success rates to drive week-over-week improvement. I would welcome the conversation.

I want to apply my skills in LLM integration and observability to elevate Airtable's customer experience at scale.
